answer: The summit multiplier is published, charged in ember, and harbor lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2402 identities would post 2287 proofs and burn roughly 52 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
